newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM CALLS FOR POSITIVE DEBATE
The Prime Minister has called for a focus on the positives of the future during a debate in the Coalition party room about the Stolen Children report.
A spokesman for the Coalition says 10 or 12 MPs spoke during the discussions, with speakers endorsing Mr Howard's stance of not issuing an offical apology.
According to the spokesman no MP called for an apology, although one MP expressed sadness the Coalition's sorrow couldn't have been expressed in more direct terms.
Mr Howard told the Party room, the only way to build a united future is to focus on the future positives, not the past negatives.
CANTERBURY TO STEP UP SECURITY AT FIXTURES FOLLOWING BRAWL
Canterbury Leagues Club has s brawl between hundreds of fans at Belmore Oval, during its Superleague match with Penrith.
Canterbury Chief Executive Bob Hagan has blamed a handful of youths for the brawl, and believes it is symptomatic of community youth problems.
Mr Hagan says club officials will meet with local community leaders to see if players can assist with problems among local youth.
Police and private security presence will be stpped up at future matches, and crowds will be monitored by video cameras.
PM SAYS VANSTONE TOOK APPROPRIATE ACTION IN CLARIFYING STATEMENT
The Prime Minister says Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone has taken the appropriate action in clarifying a previous statement on payments for job placement services.
Senator Vanstone's admitted there was a distinct possibility she misled the Senate when she said it was illegal in South Australia to charge a jobseeker for employment placement services.
The Minister says she operated in good faith and has no reason to assume she doesn't have the Prime Minister's confidence.
Shadow Employment Minister Martin Ferguson says after three cases of misleading the Senate, Mr Howard should sack his minister.
Mr Howard says Senator Vanstone had qualified her earlier statements, and Mr Ferguson may like to do the same.
He says he assumes Mr Freguson will be examining his own statement on the matter, and informing the house of any qualification he may wish to make.
PM ANNOUNCES STRATEGY TO FIGHT CRIME AND VIOLENCE
The Prime Minister has announced a new campaign which he says will be the most comprehensive strategic national approach ever undertaken to fight crime and violence.
Mr Howard says the first phase of the campaign, to be launched on Thursday, will address domestic violence, burglary, fear of crime, crime prevention and homeless youth.
He says projects, to be co-funded with the states and territories, will fulfil the Government's pre-election commitment to fight crime and violence.
Mr Howard says the strategy will also work on the genesis of criminal activity, the motivation and social determining factors behind crime and violence.
BELLS WRITES LETTER TO STAFF ABOUT POSSIBLE SALE
The management of the failed Bells Restaurants, formally Sizzlers, has written to its 2,700 workers about the chain's possible sale.
Bells management is negotiating a sale, following its sudden closure in several states yesterday.

In the letter, Bell's Managing Director, Trevor Willoughby, says redundancy payments will be part of the final creditors settlement, unless employed by the new group, which he believes will be the case.

The letter also says each manager has been asked to furnish a staff list to be forwarded to the new buyer for consideration. However, the Liquor, Hospitality and Miscellaneous Union is concerned about the workers, and is pursuing Bell's liquidator to seek a quick settlement.
TROTTING IDENTITY HIT BY DAMAGES ORDER
A leading figure in the country's trotting industry has been ordered to pay $360,000 damages following a crash during a New South Wales race meeting.
Despite acknowledging the sport's risks, the Supreme Court in Sydney today decided trainer-driver Brian Hancock breached his duty of care during the Bathurst meeting in 1992.
Fellow trainer-driver, Neville Hargreaves sued Mr Hancock after fracturing his leg and ankle when their trotting buggies collided in an accident involving three horses.
RESULTS SHOW NO BURIAL SITES AT NEERKOL
Police in Central Queensland say they will make no further investigations into claims unofficial burial sites exist at the former Sisters of Mercy Neerkol orphanage near Rockhampton.
A specialised electronic machine, an electro magntron, was used yesterday to determine if soil had been disturbed.
But it has failed to find any unmarked burial sites.
Four former residents had shown police five areas where they allege the bodies of babies had been buried.
However, Detective Inspector Russell Janke says results of the examination indicate there are no graves, and detectives are satisfied at this stage that no unofficial grave sites exist.
